clue.text: Grab, some eggs

definitions.meaning: to grab is to seize or snatch hold of something
a set of eggs laid together in one nest

explanation.surface: A terse instruction to snatch a few eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a sudden grasp, and a brood of eggs laid at one sitting.

clue.text: Local sailors involved.*in the 'opening of Irish port'?

definitions.text: Local sailors involved.*in the 'opening of Irish port

parts.words: Local sailors involved.*in the 'opening of Irish port
parts.note: the Irish port of ... would be its local sailors, and a bottle's cork is opened with a spiral tool

explanation.surface: A ship's crew helping to open a harbour in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Cork is a port in southern Ireland; read as Cork's crew it names the sailors, read as one word it is the opener for a bottle cork.
explanation.definitionFit: The spiral tool pulls a stopper from a bottle, the 'opening' the clue describes.

clue.text: " Lay not that flattering to your soul " (Hamlet)

definitions.text: " Lay not that flattering to your soul " (Hamlet)

parts.words: " Lay not that flattering to your soul " (Hamlet)
parts.note: the missing word in Hamlet's line to his mother, a soothing ointment of self-deception

explanation.surface: A line from Hamlet with a word left out.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet tells Gertrude not to soothe herself with the idea that he is mad: 'Lay not that flattering ___ to your soul'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an anointing ointment, here a comforting salve for the conscience.

clue.text: Appropriate wear if cold in the Far East.

indicators.note: in says one word is set inside the other

parts.note: China is a country of the Far East
a chill is a cold

explanation.surface: What to wear in the Far East when it gets cold.
explanation.definitionFit: The soft grey fur of the Andean rodent is used for luxury coats.

clue.text: Henry's widow among the litter-makers ? That's for the birds!

indicators.note: among says one word is set in the middle of the other

parts.note: sows are female pigs, which produce litters of piglets
Catherine Parr was the sixth wife of Henry VIII and outlived him

explanation.surface: Henry VIII's last queen among breeding pigs, dismissed as nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's for the birds' looks like the scornful idiom for something worthless, but only 'birds' defines; the rest is link padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Small brown songbirds of the finch-like family are a common example of birds.

clue.text: Outlaw the mercenary writer

parts.note: a pro, a professional, works for pay
a scribe is a writer

explanation.surface: A hired writer is banished as an outlaw.
explanation.definitionFit: To ban or forbid something formally is to prohibit it.

clue.text: Cheer up, too right !

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, says the letters read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written; that the letters also run backwards inside 'too right' is a coincidence of this R-for-right reading
R is the abbreviation for right; its letters also sit reversed in 'too right' only by coincidence

explanation.surface: An Australian-sounding cry of 'Too right!' to cheer someone up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheer up' looks like one phrase, but 'up' reverses TOO + R.
explanation.definitionFit: To root for a team is to cheer it on.

clue.text: Eviction got us in trouble

indicators.note: trouble, as a verb, stirs the letters up into a new order

explanation.surface: Being thrown out landed us in difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' reads as a phrase, but 'in' is part of the fodder and 'trouble' alone is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning someone out of their home is removing them from it.

clue.text: Add some final words on oil-containers

parts.note: to sum is to add up
PS, a postscript, is final words added to a letter

explanation.surface: An extra afterthought about oil tanks.
explanation.definitionFit: The reservoir under an engine that holds its lubricant is an oil pan.

clue.text: He takes Robert a geranium

parts.note: add Robert to a plant word starting 'He' and you get the name of a wild geranium, the cranesbill called ___ Robert

explanation.surface: A man bringing a pot plant for Robert.
explanation.walkthrough: The wild geranium Geranium robertianum is commonly named after Robert; the first word of its name, a general plant term, begins with the clue's 'He'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant valued for flavour or medicine, as the wild cranesbill is.

clue.text: Exotic queen about 150? Lie !

indicators.note: about says the queen's word goes round the number

parts.note: reine is French for queen, so a foreign queen
CL is 150 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A foreign queen of about 150 is accused of lying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exotic' tempts as an anagram signal, but here it marks a foreign word: the queen is French.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie back on a sofa is to lean back or rest at full length.

clue.text: I exclaim my classic ability to feign death

parts.note: O is an exclamation, the cry 'Oh!'
possum is Latin, a classical language, for 'I am able'

explanation.surface: Someone boasting, with a cry, of a talent for playing dead.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the creature's habit: to 'play possum' is to feign death, the trick the American marsupial is famous for.
explanation.definitionFit: The American marsupial is known for lying motionless as if dead when threatened.

clue.text: Change in return for the fun of the fair

parts.note: to switch is to change over
back means in return, as in paying someone back

explanation.surface: Exchanging something to get the enjoyment of a funfair.
explanation.walkthrough: A switchback is an old British name for a roller coaster, a funfair ride.
explanation.definitionFit: A roller-coaster ride with steep ups and downs is a classic amusement at a funfair.

clue.text: Wood has such prejudice

definitions.meaning: a wood is a bowl in the game of bowls, weighted to curve on its run

explanation.surface: Someone called Wood is said to hold a prejudice.
explanation.walkthrough: Wood looks like a surname, but in bowls (a lawn game) a 'wood' is a ball, built off-centre so it curves.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowl's off-centre weighting and a person's partiality are both a leaning to one side.

clue.text: Temperature with possibility of some inflammation?

definitions.text: Temperature with possibility of some inflammation?

parts.words: Temperature with possibility of some inflammation
parts.note: the lowest heat at which a liquid's vapour can ignite, dressed up as a medical fever

explanation.surface: A fever warning of an inflamed wound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Temperature' and 'inflammation' suggest illness, but the inflammation is catching fire.
explanation.definitionFit: The ignition threshold of a vapour, also used for the point where tension erupts.

clue.text: Rapid progress in uninterrupted succession

definitions.meaning: moving at a run, quick going
as in 'three days on the trot', one after another

explanation.surface: Quick advance achieved without a single break.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprinting is fast movement, and 'five times on end' uses the same word for consecutive.

clue.text: See perhaps a GI return with this decoration

indicators.note: perhaps says the letters may be put in some other order

explanation.surface: A returning American soldier brings home an ornament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges A GI RETURN; 'See' and 'with this' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A garnish or ornamental set of trimmings adorning something.

clue.text: That .Latin lass 'is breaking' the law

parts.note: ille is the Latin word for that
gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: A girl from Latium caught committing a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unlawful is against the law, so doing it is breaking the law.

clue.text: A.' foothold for masonic members on the square

parts.note: Freemasons meet in lodges, so lodge men are masonic members
a T-square is a drawing tool, so T is the square

explanation.surface: Freemasons get their start by being on the level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the square' is Masonic jargon for honest, but here gives T, from the T-square; 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A position gained and held, as troops secure ground in enemy territory.

clue.text: Bird when returned is about a pound uncooked

indicators.note: returned means the assembled string of words is read backwards

parts.note: re means about, concerning
lb is the abbreviation for a pound weight
raw food is uncooked

explanation.surface: A bird sent back because it was a pound of raw meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when returned' turns the whole run RE + LB + RAW, giving the letters backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A songbird of the Old World family Sylviidae, known for trilling song.

clue.text: News of firings ?

definitions.meaning: accounts of events, as published by journalists
the bangs of guns being fired

explanation.surface: Coverage of people being sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firings' suggests dismissals, but means shots, the loud bangs of guns.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: written accounts of events, and explosive noises from gunfire.

clue.text: Stored like linseed, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps says the word is one possible arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: Kept away for later, as one might keep flax seed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges LINSEED; 'like' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Fodder kept in a silo for the winter has been put into store.

clue.text: Like Ethiopia's emperor vis-à-vis Judah

parts.note: Haile Selassie held the title 'Lion of Judah', so in that respect he was lion-like

explanation.surface: Comparing Haile Selassie with the tribe of Judah.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means resembling a lion, the beast of the emperor's title.

clue.text: N European circuit, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: a lap is one circuit of a track

explanation.surface: Talk of a lap round a track somewhere in northern Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sami people of northern Scandinavia are traditionally called by this older name.

clue.text: While one is out of practice, he is in

definitions.text: While one is out of practice, he is in

parts.words: While one is out of practice, he is in
parts.note: when a doctor is away from the surgery, a stand-in doctor works in their practice

explanation.surface: A rusty player is replaced by a substitute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of practice' suggests being rusty, but means away from one's medical practice.
explanation.definitionFit: A temporary doctor standing in for an absent colleague.

clue.text: Take dim view of difficult Ovid papers

indicators.note: difficult suggests the letters are in a tangled state needing sorting

explanation.surface: Frowning on the hard essays about the Roman poet Ovid.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a dim view is to frown on or not approve of something.

clue.text: See 30 ac
Music-maker has honour without love

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the honour wraps round

parts.note: the OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire
love is zero in tennis, so O

explanation.surface: A musician given an award but lonely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without love' reads as loveless, but 'without' means outside: OBE goes round O.
explanation.definitionFit: A double-reed woodwind instrument plays music.

clue.text: Reindeer's a West Indian type, nothing high-class

parts.note: the Carib are an indigenous people of the Caribbean islands
O is the round figure zero, so nothing
U is a British label for upper-class usage

explanation.surface: A reindeer described as a Caribbean sort, and not posh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nothing high-class' reads as an insult, but splits into O and U.
explanation.definitionFit: The North American reindeer goes by this name.

clue.text: Source of dye is a duck in the Orient

parts.note: a duck is a score of zero in cricket, so nil
E stands for east, the Orient

explanation.surface: A dye said to come from a duck in the Far East.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck in cricket is a batter's score of nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: This chemical is the base for many synthetic colouring agents.

clue.text: Sounds hot stuff gets us, summoned

indicators.note: Sounds says the word is heard, not seen written

parts.note: mustard is a hot condiment

explanation.surface: A spicy condiment calls us together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets us' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops gathered or called together for inspection have been assembled.

clue.text: Urban waif, not only in Mecca

definitions.text: Urban waif, not only in Mecca

parts.words: Urban waif, not only in Mecca
parts.note: a homeless city child; such children are found not only in Arabia but in any city road

explanation.surface: Homeless city children exist far beyond Saudi Arabia.
explanation.walkthrough: The old phrase for a ragged child living rough in a city ends in a word for a native of Arabia, hence the Mecca reference.
explanation.definitionFit: Victorian term for a homeless child roaming city roads.
